title: Parallel trace writer pool + adaptive backpressure to reduce span-ingest tail latency
creator: Alex Chen
description: Problem: trace ingestion pipeline shows intermittent high tail latency (p99 export spikes >1s) caused by single-threaded export writer, unbounded queueing, and allocation-heavy span encoding. Goal: implement a parallel writer pool with bounded per-worker queues and adaptive backpressure to stabilize p99 latency and reduce allocation pressure.
technical_approach: 1) Add configurable fixed-size writer pool where each worker has a bounded ring buffer. 2) Replace hot-path JSON encoder with pooled buffer encoder and compact binary marshalling for internal exports (JSON preserved behind flag). 3) Implement adaptive backpressure: throttle low-priority spans when queue fullness crosses high-water marks and emit exporter_shed events. 4) Provide trace prioritization (errors/high-latency elevated, health-checks deprioritized). 5) Add runtime knobs: pool_size, per_writer_queue_capacity, backpressure thresholds, enable_binary_encoder. 6) Preserve API compatibility with OTLP exporters and provide ordering-preservation mode for traces requiring strict ordering.
acceptance_criteria: - p99 export latency <200ms on standard 10k RPS synthetic workload. - Span encoder allocs per-span reduced by >=50% in microbenchmarks. - No lost diagnostic/error spans during normal operation; shed events visible and small under nominal load. - All features behind runtime flags for quick rollback. - Canary rollout executed with sign-off at each stage. - Unit and integration tests added for pool, queues, and prioritization.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and enable in staging. 2) Canary: 1% traces in us-west-2 for 24h, validate latency/memory/CPU/no data loss. 3) Ramp to 10% for 12h with extended load tests (inject exporter latency and errors). 4) Ramp to 50% for 48h. 5) Full rollout. Rollback by disabling feature flag; if disk-backed circuit triggers often, reduce ingestion upstream and investigate exporters.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for ring buffer semantics and backpressure signals. - Integration test with fake exporter that injects latency/errors to validate shed and fallback. - Microbenchmarks for encoder allocs. - Perf env load tests at target RPS with span size distributions. - Chaos tests: exporter delays, OOM simulator, network partitions. - Data validation comparing span samples pre/post-change for integrity and ordering.
metrics_and_kpis: - span_export_p50/95/99 latency (ms); span_ingest_queue_length per-worker; span_encoder_alloc_bytes per-span; exporter_shed_events; exporter_error_rate and retry_rate; memory RSS and GC pause; CPU utilization. Targets: p99 <200ms, encoder allocs -50%, exporter_shed_events minimal under nominal load.
risks: - Potential span reordering within traces if prioritization moves spans across writers. - Data loss risk if backpressure wrongly classifies spans to shed. - Increased binary complexity and size from extra encoders and pooling. - Downstream exporters may expect serial ordering causing compatibility issues.
mitigations: - Implement ordering-preservation mode for dependent traces. - Conservative default shed policy (only low-signal spans). - Feature flags for encoder selection and pool tuning. - Extensive canarying and load testing before wide rollout. - Surge playbook in runbook for post-deploy issues.
